resources.string: Allow precise location to list networks. Android requires it to read Wi-Fi scan results; NetKit does not use it to determine location.
Turn on system Location, then scan again.
The new scan was not confirmed; Android probably throttled scanning. The data keeps its original time.
The scan was cancelled; the data is from the previous scan.
No results are available yet. Check permissions, Location and Wi-Fi, then scan.

Android limits scan frequency (typically 4 per 2 minutes for a foreground app). NetKit scans only when you tap the button; cached data is never presented as a new scan. For local testing, this limit can be changed in Developer options.
Locally administered BSSID; vendor cannot be identified from the OUI.
OUI vendor unavailable (no verified database bundled).
Each AP trapezoid shows channel width and RSSI from the last scan. The chart draws at most 6 APs (always the connected one); the list and scores include all of them.
The data is unconfirmed or older than 5 minutes. A new scan will show channel health.
No AP was found in this band. The phone may not scan it; an empty band does not mean free channels.

Channel health is an estimate from the overlap of visible networks and from the utilization APs themselves advertise in the BSS Load element (many home routers do not send it). It does not measure airtime or interference from non-Wi-Fi devices.
The phone is not connected to Wi-Fi. Measuring resumes once connected.
Without precise location permission Android hides the SSID and BSSID. Signal and latency are still measured, but roaming cannot be detected. Grant the permission on the Wi-Fi analyzer screen.
System location is off, so Android hides the SSID and BSSID. Turn location on to track roaming.
This device does not allow unprivileged ICMP echo; latency cannot be measured.
The Wi-Fi network has no IPv4 default gateway; gateway latency cannot be measured.
This device does not provide traffic counters; throughput cannot be shown.
DNS did not answer within 2 s
Enter a numeric IPv4 address, for example 1.1.1.1.
Enter a valid domain name, for example one.one.one.one.
